title: hand egg beater
description: A hand crank turns a big gear that turns two small gears, each carrying a beater blade that stirs a bowl of batter; no motor, hands or kitchen shown

facts.intro: Introduce a recognizable hand egg beater: a red crank on a big brass gear, two small steel gears below it each carrying a beater blade, and a bowl of yellow batter underneath. Everything is still.
facts.cutaway: Inside are the big brass gear, and the two small steel gears whose teeth mesh with it, each with a blade fixed to its axle.
facts.drive: A push turns the crank and the big gear. Its teeth drive both small gears round, and the two blades spin through the batter.
facts.response: The crank keeps turning. The big gear has three times as many teeth as each small gear, so each blade spins three times for every turn of the crank.
facts.hold: No part moves for this explanation. The big gear has twenty-four teeth and each small gear has eight, so one crank turn spins each blade three times.
facts.repeat: A second push turns the crank again. The blades whirl faster than the crank and keep stirring the batter in step.
facts.limit: The crank turns backwards for a moment. Both blades reverse as well, because the gears stay locked together tooth to tooth.
facts.payoff: Crank, big gear, small gears and blades work together: one slow turn of the handle becomes three fast spins of both blades. No motor or hand is shown.
